title: valid negative_gamma interpretation (host-authored)

observations: Net gamma exposure is negative: dealers are net short gamma across the chain, so their hedging follows the direction of price rather than leaning against it.
Spot is trading below the zero-gamma level and sitting on the put wall, which places the market in the part of the profile where dealer hedging is destabilizing.
Put gamma dominates call gamma by a wide margin, consistent with heavy downside protection being held by end clients.
implications: While spot stays below the zero-gamma level, intraday moves are more likely to be amplified than dampened; a reclaim of that level would flip dealers back toward a stabilizing posture.
The put wall is the nearest concentration of put gamma below spot; if it fails, hedging flows can accelerate the move rather than absorb it.
The call wall sits above the zero-gamma level and marks where call gamma would cap a rebound if the regime turned positive.

evidence.claim: Net gamma exposure is negative, so dealers are net short gamma
Spot is below the zero-gamma level
Spot is sitting on the put wall
The call wall is above the zero-gamma level

limitations: This is a point-in-time snapshot of open interest; new flow, expirations rolling off and intraday hedging can change the profile quickly.
Coverage is complete for the requested expirations, but the profile only reflects listed options gamma and says nothing about other sources of dealer hedging.
The near-zero regime cannot be assessed by the validator because GaleCore publishes call and put gamma on a different scale than net gamma.
